user.title: Swiss Solar Forecast
user.description: Where is the plant? Your Home Assistant location is pre-filled: move the marker onto the roof, or type a street address (the federal address register knows every address of Switzerland). The next step lists the roof planes of that building from the Sonnendach cadastre of the Federal Office of Energy; you tick every plane that carries modules, then enter the figures of each plane one after the other. One entry is the whole plant.

roofs.title: Roof planes
roofs.description: {count} roof plane(s) at {place} in the Sonnendach cadastre, largest first: orientation, tilt, area, suitability class (1 low … 5 top) and the long-term electricity yield of the whole plane. Tick every plane that carries modules. The last entry (✎) adds a plane you enter by hand, for a roof the cadastre does not know, a garage on another building or a ground-mounted plant; tick it together with the others if you need both.

plane.title: Plane {index} of {total}
plane.description: Roof: {roof}. Orientation and tilt come from the cadastre; correct them if you know better. Enter the installed peak power of this plane in kWp (the cadastre's area would hold about {kwp_hint} kWp with modern modules). Losses cover wiring, inverter, soiling and mismatch (14 % is a usual figure). The inverter limit clips this plane's AC power (0 = none). Damping scales the result, for calibration against your real yield.

reconfigure.title: Move the plant or change its planes
reconfigure.description: Move the marker or type another address; the roof planes there are listed next (the plant's current planes are pre-ticked), then the figures of every plane with the current values pre-filled. The entry keeps its entities, their ids and history.

reconfigure_roofs.title: Roof planes
reconfigure_roofs.description: {count} roof plane(s) at {place} in the Sonnendach cadastre, largest first. Tick every plane that carries modules; the last entry (✎) adds a plane entered by hand.

reconfigure_plane.title: Plane {index} of {total}
reconfigure_plane.description: Roof: {roof}. The figures are the plane's current ones where the plant already had this roof, else the cadastre's suggestion.

error.cannot_connect: The federal geo service could not be reached. Check the internet connection and try again.
error.no_match: No address matches the text. Try street and place, or move the marker instead.
error.pick_one: Tick at least one plane, or the pencil for a plane entered by hand.

abort.already_configured: A plant at this place is already set up. Use its Reconfigure to change the planes.
abort.cannot_connect: The MeteoSwiss open data could not be read. Check the internet connection and try again.

init.title: Which plane?
init.description: The plant's planes. Pick the one whose figures you want to change. To add or remove planes, or move the plant, use Reconfigure in the entry's menu.

plane.title: Plane {plane}
plane.description: Peak power, orientation, tilt, losses, inverter limit and damping of this plane. Changing a value reloads the entry; entity ids and history are kept. Use damping to calibrate: if the forecast is 10 % too high over a few sunny weeks, set 0.9.

abort.no_planes: This plant has no planes; set it up again.

forecast_unreachable.title: Swiss Solar Forecast: forecast not readable
forecast_unreachable.description: The MeteoSwiss open data could not be read for several refreshes in a row ({error}). Check your internet connection; if it is fine, the MeteoSwiss service is down or has changed. The sensors stay unavailable until then and recover on their own; this notice disappears with the next successful refresh.
